主要内容: Qualcomm (QCOM) reported its first-quarter 2022 earnings on Wednesday, beating analyst expectations for revenue and guidance. The company's chip business grew 35% year-over-year, driven by strong handset chip sales. Qualcomm's revenue reached $10.7 billion, up 30% from the previous year, with an EPS of $3.23, exceeding the $3.01 expected. The company also raised its sales forecast for the upcoming quarter, projecting between $10.2 billion and $11 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $9.6 billion. Qualcomm's chip division, QCT, reported $8.85 billion in sales, up 35% from the same quarter last year. The growth highlights the continued demand for advanced microchips. CEO Cristiano Amon noted that supply improvements are being seen, but demand still outpaces supply. Qualcomm's various divisions, including automotive, IoT, and RF front-end, all showed growth, with the IoT division increasing sales by 41% to $1.48 billion. Qualcomm reported its Q1 2022 earnings, highlighting a 10% year-over-year increase in revenue for its QTL division, which reached $1.81 billion. The company also mentioned that it had not included gains from its QSI investment division in its GAAP earnings forecast for the second quarter due to market volatility. During the quarter, QSI contributed $0.10 to its GAAP earnings per share. Qualcomm repurchased $1.2 billion in shares and issued $765 million in dividends. The company emphasized its strength in tackling everything as a system, as stated by its CEO.
